articleTitle: Enhancing Secure Cross-Border Collaboration among Law Enforcement Agencies for Facial Biometric Search
publicationTitle: 2024 5th International Conference in Electronic Engineering, Information Technology & Education (EEITE)
abstract: Addressing the growing challenge of combating international crime involves the development of secure and efficient methodologies that allow Law Enforcement Agencies to exchange information seamlessly, without being hindered by time-consuming bureaucratic processes. In this context, we present a solution centered on facial biometric search methodologies. Our approach underscores the importance of employing accurate and reliable methods to assess image data similarity, particularly in the domain of facial images, which pose unique challenges due to subtle variations. We propose a comprehensive solution that harnesses hashing techniques and homomorphic encryption. By doing so, our approach ensures secure data exchange while safeguarding confidentiality and integrity. We firmly believe that our approach will substantially improve collaboration in law enforcement efforts and make significant contributions to global security.

articleTitle: Pedagogical Innovation in Higher Education Using an Active Learning Methodology to Increase the Effectiveness of Geometry Learning for Engineering Students
publicationTitle: 2024 5th International Conference in Electronic Engineering, Information Technology & Education (EEITE)
abstract: Pedagogical innovation in higher education using an active learning methodology to increase the effectiveness of geometry learning for engineering students. Active methodologies have been used in the most varied disciplines with the aim of teaching the syllabus to students in an active way. Engineering students like to learn by doing, having an aptitude for technology. Applying active methodologies to teach mathematics to engineers is an added value. The study presented applies active methodologies to increase the effectiveness of geometry learning for engineering students. An innovative pedagogical activity was developed with the support of technologies: GeoGebra and augmented reality. 38 students carried out this activity in the classroom under the guidance and monitoring of the teacher. Before the activity, they answered a questionnaire and another after the activity. From the information collected in the two questionnaires and the participants observation by the teacher in the classroom, analyses and reflections were carried out. As a result, it was found that the methodology presented in this study shows that it is possible to promote the development of skills with active learning, in innovative activities, awakening students' curiosity and allowing them to study independently, which is one of the characteristics of the 21st century students.

articleTitle: Synthesis and Analysis of a Novel Parameterized Morphing, Honeycomb Cellular Cell Propulsion Actuation System of an AUV
publicationTitle: 2024 5th International Conference in Electronic Engineering, Information Technology & Education (EEITE)
abstract: This paper presents a parametric novel design of a distributed propulsion actuation system, oriented for applications in morphing for Autonomous Underwater Vehicles (AUV) structures. A novel design of a morphing parameterized motion actuation mechanism is proposed, in order to compose the internal structural layout. The governing principals regarding the cellular honeycomb core, which our propulsion actuation system is composed, are interdependent by the cell parameters of the layout. The analysis model developed, responds to the following criteria. First, it must allow a wide displacement ratio with regards to its rigid body. Second, a variation in planform area, taking into account the minimum strain on structural members, is mandatory in order to have numerical stability, crucial factor of the finite element analysis. For display purposes, the parametric morphing actuation mechanism model is featured. In compliant, the morphing structure design contributes in adaptable, lightweight and high load carrying capability of an Autonomous Underwater Vehicles (AUVs). Finally, FEM analysis with an appropriate number of elements is created, in order to accurately capture the localized material fatigue constraints, as well as to study the behavior of the parametric mechanism under stress due to high pressure.

articleTitle: Evaluating the Performance of a MIMO Channel Under Tree Shadowing for Low-Altitude UAVs
publicationTitle: 2024 5th International Conference in Electronic Engineering, Information Technology & Education (EEITE)
abstract: This article assesses the performance of a dual-polarized (DP) multiple-input-multiple-output (MIMO) communication link, between a low-altitude unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) and a terrestrial terminal. The entire analysis is based on experiments that are commenced in an urban park, having trees that shadow the wireless link. The ergodic capacities are calculated 5.1 and 4.3 b/s/Hz, for line-of-sight (LOS) and non-line-of-sight (NLOS) trajectories, respectively. The obtained results demonstrated that the ergodic capacity, as well as the K-factor of the DP-MIMO channel, vary substantially with respect to the elevation angle. Based on the channel decomposition results and its correlation properties, the communication link under consideration is suitable to accommodate either beamforming, or diversity, instead of spatial multiplexing.

articleTitle: Conventional versus Reinforced Additive Manufacturing in Unmanned Aerial Vehicle Design
publicationTitle: 2024 5th International Conference in Electronic Engineering, Information Technology & Education (EEITE)
abstract: Additive manufacturing has significantly impacted the research and development of Unmanned Aerial Vehicles, enabling rapid prototyping and fast production. A framework for designing and manufacturing parts of specialized multirotor UAVs is considered, incorporating the process of mechanical testing of 3D printed specimens. Based on material testing, it is possible to construct parts with the required mechanical properties while retaining a lightweight and low-cost airframe. Tests were conducted on five series of specimens that were 3D printed with a different combination of technologies, materials, and parameters. The results are shown graphically, and mechanical properties can be compared for further testing and use in aircraft design.

articleTitle: A Naive Bayes Classifier for Fault Detection and Classification Using Dimension Reduction Technique
publicationTitle: 2024 5th International Conference in Electronic Engineering, Information Technology & Education (EEITE)
abstract: Fault detection and classification is critical to the reliability of modern control systems in different industries, where detecting and classifying faults in operational processes are very important things while failure to detect and classify them, may cause irreparable damage. In this paper, fault detection and classification approach is presented. The first step, multi stage recursive least squares parameter estimation approach for controlled autoregressive autoregressive moving average systems (CARARMA) is developed with a view to estimate the parameters of the system, additionally, improve the effectiveness of the computation. By means of multi stage approach, the (CARARMA) system is decomposed into three simple identification models, and the parameters of each simple model is identified one by one. These parameters estimated by this approach are referred to as features, and not all of them have the same useful data about the system. In order to select the valuable features and improve a classification accuracy, the Linear Discriminant Analysis (LDA) approach based on scattering matrices is applied for dimension reduction. The classification between these reduced classes is done based on the Naive Bayes classifier. Finally, the obtained results explain the performance of this proposed approach.

articleTitle: Exploring HEIs Students' Perceptions of Artificial Intelligence on their Learning Process
publicationTitle: 2024 5th International Conference in Electronic Engineering, Information Technology & Education (EEITE)
abstract: An increasing number of colleges and universities are introducing Generative Artificial Intelligence (GAI) in their teaching/learning frameworks. This study examines the feedback from 152 students across Higher Education Institutions (HEIs), representing diverse scientific areas, namely Engineering, Lit-erature, Business and Accounting, Sports. It aims to explore the integration of GAI features in education and students' perception on its advantages and disadvantages. Students' top benefit was ‘Personalized learning’. They also valued ‘efficient content creation’, and ‘individualized assessment tools’. Their major concern was ‘Ethical considerations‘, and it varied by demographic variables. Other distresses included ‘Lack of control of content creation’, ‘over-reliance’, and ‘AI depersonalization’, and ‘decreased interpersonal engagement’. Of utmost important conclusion is that HE students agree and strongly agree that AI came to disrupt HEIs' educational process.

articleTitle: Performance Comparison of Organic Transistors with Different Poly(3-Hexyl Thiophene) Solvents
publicationTitle: 2024 5th International Conference in Electronic Engineering, Information Technology & Education (EEITE)
abstract: Poly(3-hexylthiophene) (P3HT) as an active layer (organic semiconductor) in organic transistors is of particular interest due to its self-organizing properties to form a microcrystalline structure. Intensive research to improve carrier mobility by several orders of magnitude has shown that the morphology of the organic material is critically affected by the regioregularity, molecular weight, molecular weight distribution and chain stiffness, as well as processing conditions. Many studies have shown that deposition methods, solubility and boiling point of the solvent affect the semiconductor morphology. Boiling point in particular seems to be of obvious importance, since high boiling point solvents evaporate more slowly. This increased evaporation period then gives the polymer chains more time to arrange themselves into a better crystal structure (crystallization) and therefore better performing devices. In this work, the importance of the active layer solvent (P3HT) is demonstrated, by comparing the laboratory results of two classes of devices that after P3HT deposition were baked at the same temperature and time under vacuum and room conditions respectively.

articleTitle: Perceptions of International Students in a Higher Education Institute in Sweden
publicationTitle: 2024 5th International Conference in Electronic Engineering, Information Technology & Education (EEITE)
abstract: The process of internationalising higher education brings about numerous benefits f or t eaching a nd l earning activities. It fosters an extensive exchange of information that extends beyond national borders. Nonetheless, achieving an acceptable standard of quality to meet the expectations of international students necessitates diligent feedback and inquiry to comprehend and address their experiences effectively. This work's primary objective is to investigate international students experiences, focusing on factors that can influence t h eir a c ademic pursuits, including learning activities, learning environment, academic collaboration and social integration at a higher education institute in Sweden. This study employs a quantitative analysis methodology to examine anonymous surveys completed by a group of international students at our university. The gathered data were classified i n to t h ree d i stinct c a tegories a n d subjected to separate analyses within each category. The findings suggest that the expectations of international students are met mainly regarding learning activities, receiving the highest score. However, challenges were observed in the learning environment, especially with regard to academic collaboration and social integration with domestic students. Recommendations for improvement include promoting social integration, enhancing academic collaboration, improving information dissemination, and establishing partnerships with the municipality to ensure better accommodation. These findings offer valuable insights for our university and other institutions striving to enhance international students' educational quality and overall experience.

articleTitle: HEIs teachers' and students' current experience of AI introduction in teaching and learning
publicationTitle: 2024 5th International Conference in Electronic Engineering, Information Technology & Education (EEITE)
abstract: Higher Education Institutions (HEIs) are increasingly incorporating artificial i ntelligence (AI) into their learning setup. In this paper, we analyze the results of a survey posed to 152 Higher Education (HE) students and 136 HE educators, of different scientific b ackgrounds, to emphasize the current incorporation of AI in the teaching and learning processes. The results reveal distinct viewpoints from both parties, reflecting diversified l evels o f e xperience, presumptions, and uneasiness. Thirty two percent of the teachers, completing the survey, confirms using AI. Approximately 50% reveal they notice their students using AI to (i) automate routine tasks in or out-ofclass, including check correctness of answers, obtaining real-time feedback; (ii) personalize learning tasks, such as write essays or projects and to illustrate them, and create presentations. A smaller percentage reveals students using AI to produce video content and contrast information learned in class. Alternative means, encompassing using AI at home, to study, to gather information, to sum up ideas in texts, are identified by most teachers as being employed by their students. Students using AI outnumber the teachers, though there are significant d ifferences in some responses, when compared to the teachers' perceptions, for the sames questions. Most of the students prefer AI to study at home, to obtain information to improve or to check an answer. Then a significant number does not exploit AI either to create presentations, write an essay or project, illustrate a project, producing videos, or to contrast information obtained in classes with that collected by AI tools. Regardless of these differences, both parties agree and strongly agree (with 79% of students and 86% of teachers) that AI will affect the HEIs educational process in the future.

articleTitle: Footprint of Semantics in ICT
publicationTitle: 2024 5th International Conference in Electronic Engineering, Information Technology & Education (EEITE)
abstract: In this paper we have been reviewing the incorporation of Semantics in various Information and Communication Technologies (ICT). Our extensive literature search resulted in a wide range of ICT applications in various fields. A set of requirements is necessary for the successful integration of semantics. The advantages and disadvantages of such an incorporation are pointed out, followed by the conclusions and a series of open issues that will absorb our future research efforts.

articleTitle: Design of Virtual Vehicle System with Mechanical Steering Response
publicationTitle: 2024 5th International Conference in Electronic Engineering, Information Technology & Education (EEITE)
abstract: This paper presents an introspection into the world of simulating vehicle responses from a virtual environment and developing and designing a system to recreate those responses in the real world. Using sophisticated electronic and mechanical control, combined with readily available components, a method is demonstrated for providing realistic feedback to the user. With the use of rapid prototyping techniques along with 3D modelling specific geometries, mechanical interactions were able to be incorporated into the final prototype. The electronic control is based on field-oriented control which provides the system with a highly flexible and stable response in a closed loop manner.

articleTitle: Secret Code: A STEAM Project to Teach Mathematics in Higher Education
publicationTitle: 2024 5th International Conference in Electronic Engineering, Information Technology & Education (EEITE)
abstract: STEAM teaching is based on experimentation and the insertion of new technologies, cultivating students' investigation, dialogue, and critical thinking. This methodology allows to respond to contemporary challenges, through the promotion of transdisciplinary, associated with the resolution of real problems. The skills linked to the integrated scientific approach: Science, Technology, Engineering, [Art] and Mathematics (STEAM), are very important in integrating more active learning with a better understanding of scientific content. This work describes and analyses the use of a pedagogical practice using the active STEAM methodology, in a classroom context, in which students are the protagonists of their own learning. In this learning process, students develop self-confidence, self-esteem, and autonomy to learn. In December 2023, 16 and 21 students from the degrees in Electromechanical Engineering and Biomedical Engineering, respectively, for 4 hours, were invited to develop an activity entitled “Use matrices to encode and decode secret messages”, prepare a report and answer to two questionnaires (pre and post activity involvement). As a result of the analysis (direct observation and questionnaires application) it was found that learning mathematics, mediated by digital technologies, allows the development of content in an effective and agile way for students. The increase in problem-solving capacity was evident in all observations, followed by the interaction capacity that the use of active methodologies provides. The positive factors such as motivation, learning and development of soft and hard skills of the students involved allowed us to realize that an integrated or interdisciplinary curriculum, as a pedagogical strategy like this, prioritizes the quality of teaching.

articleTitle: Thermal Anomalies Related to the Devastating Mw7 Earthquake of Samos ‒ Izmir (October 30, 2020) Using Long-Term Satellite Data Analysis
publicationTitle: 2024 5th International Conference in Electronic Engineering, Information Technology & Education (EEITE)
abstract: On October 30, 2020, 11:51:27 UTC, an intense and destructive earthquake of Mw7 hit the Greek Aegean Island of Samos and Turkey's western coastline close to the city of Izmir, resulting to serious structure damage, 119 fatalities and over 15000 homeless. Approximately 40 aftershocks with M>4, including one strong aftershock (Mw=5.2), followed the major seismic event the same day, while a tsunami event was recorded the following hours to days. Only three moderate foreshocks (M3.2 & M3) were recorded in the adjustment area during a period of sixty days before the main seismic event, while over 400 aftershocks with M>3 occurred the 2 following months. Our aim is to detect and map land surface thermal anomalies preceded the major event. The Robust Satellite Technique was coupled with a dataset consisting of eleven years (2010-2020) of daily MODIS-LST satellite images and as a result RETIRA index was computed. During the preliminary analysis 10 preseismic thermal anomalies (TAs) that occurred 60 to 2 days before the catastrophic tectonic event were detected.

articleTitle: Cobalt Catalyst Hysteresis Loop Simulations: The Impact of Nanoparticle Number and Nearest Neighbor Distance
publicationTitle: 2024 5th International Conference in Electronic Engineering, Information Technology & Education (EEITE)
abstract: This study investigates the magnetization of Cobalt (Co) nanoparticles with two different crystal structures: a centered cubic (fcc) and a hexagonal close packed (hcp), under the magnetic field of the Earth. For both samples, the nanoparticle number variation and the nearest neighbor distance effect, in the Co hysteresis loop are investigated, structural information that is useful for the sample preparation. The two samples are simulated using Finite Element Method (FEM) and their hysteresis loops are exported. From the simulation, it is proven that, for both samples, the nanoparticle number effect does not change the hysteresis loop. In contrast, when the distance between the nanoparticles increases, the magnetization is lowered. In addition, experiments are conducted that validate the magnetization values of the hysteresis loops in the region of the terrestrial magnetic field. The measurement set-up is based on fluxgate magnetometers. In this article, the experimental validation is focused on the magnetization values close to the earth magnetic field, while the validation of other points of the hysteresis loops will be discussed in a future publication. The final goal is to be created a methodology for both spatial and temporal resolution of the magnetic phase of the catalyst, a fact very important for the field of chemical reactions. This study aims to propose a novel, simple, and economical measurement arrangement enabling in situ magnetic measurements for ferromagnetic nano-material characterization.

articleTitle: Sarcopenia detection with portable ultrasound
publicationTitle: 2024 5th International Conference in Electronic Engineering, Information Technology & Education (EEITE)
abstract: Recent advancements in healthcare show that machine learning models can be used in clinical practice, embedded into assisting tools, aiming to enhance the experience of both patients and clinicians. Specifically in the field of disease monitoring and improving the QoL of patients, applications are being developed to be tailored to each patient's symptoms to produce personal recommendations. This study focuses on the development of a tool designed to monitor sarcopenia, a disease characterized by muscle wasting and malnutrition, in this case in advanced pancreatic cancer patients. The aim is to develop a multimodal approach, utilizing measurements from electronic health records (EHR), the measurement of a hand-held dynamometer and the 4m walking stride, alongside muscle ultrasound images from the biceps branchii, to measure the muscle thickness and estimate the stage of the disease. The ultimate goal of using portable ultrasound devices for disease monitoring, combined with AI tools, is cutting down expensive and time-consuming exams, as well as providing selfmanagement of the disease. This study falls on but is not limited to the scope of the Horizon RELEVIUM Project.

articleTitle: Integrals Applications: A STEAM Activity to Teach/Learn Mathematics in Higher Education
publicationTitle: 2024 5th International Conference in Electronic Engineering, Information Technology & Education (EEITE)
abstract: STEAM education comprehends experimentation and the integration of cutting-edge technologies to foster students' inquiry, dialogue, and critical thinking skills. This pedagogical approach addresses contemporary challenges by promoting transdisciplinary learning and problem-solving in real-world contexts. The integration of Science, Technology, Engineering, Art, and Mathematics (STEAM) enriches active learning methodologies and enhances students' understanding of scientific concepts. This paper examines the implementation of an active STEAM methodology in a learning environment that may be set as a classroom or implemented as a game. In whatever environment chosen, students take centre stage in their learning journey. Through this approach, students not only gain confidence and self-esteem but also develop autonomy in their learning process. Students are invited to dimension and plan to rebuild a city that was destroyed by some catastrophe. The planning activity is part of a game where the main aim is to acquire knowledge about integrals and their usage. As a result, we may infer that learning mathematics, mediated by digital technologies, allows the development of content in an effective and agile way for students. The increase in problem-solving, communication between peers, and the use of technological tools are competencies that may be evaluated during the execution of this activity. The students' motivation, learning, and development of soft and hard skills allowed us to realize that an integrated or interdisciplinary curriculum, as a pedagogical strategy like this, improves teaching quality and the learning process.

articleTitle: Simulation Software for Heat and Power Cogeneration (CHP) Using Green Hydrogen
publicationTitle: 2024 5th International Conference in Electronic Engineering, Information Technology & Education (EEITE)
abstract: Energy transition offers a wide range of benefits, including the potential to confront the recent energy crisis. Green hydrogen is a fast-developing clean energy source due to its low carbon emission in the atmosphere, promoting, thus, not only significant economic growth, but also independence from fossil fuels. Raising the public's awareness about renewable energy sources can lead to social acceptance and the rise of green practices, leading to the assimilation of such practices into everyday occurrences. To increase these practices and educate both students and the public about renewable energy, the role of educational establishments is considered essential. An effective tool to spread awareness and provide insight about green hydrogen is through specialized simulation software. In this paper, an interactive dashboard is realized to examine, to a certain extent, how a hybrid battery-hydrogen storage system operates and satisfies different energy needs, using photovoltaics, water electrolysis and fuel cells, implemented using Microsoft Excel® and its integrated tools. By processing a sample of load data originated from a hotel located in Heraklion, Greece and some user-defined variables, the software calculates hourly values including hydrogen and thermal production in an annual basis.

articleTitle: The SElectively Integrated Returns Intelligent Optimisation System — SEIRIOS
publicationTitle: 2024 5th International Conference in Electronic Engineering, Information Technology & Education (EEITE)
abstract: Further advancing the Optimal Returns IntegratiOnal Network — ORION, Loukeris (2023), the diagnosis of bubbles and their potential returns is produced innovatively to elaborate significant parameters of the portfolio optimization domain, such as: i) trends on investors patterns, ii) the Entropic effect on investors in the Chaotic effects of the Markets in SDEs by Tsallis Statistics and the FMH - Fractal Market Hypothesis, iii) to detect an optimal classifier on 60 Modular Networks of Neurals or Hybrid Neuro-Genetics to support the optimal asset allocation policy, are examined. The SElectively Integrated Returns Intelligent Optimisation System — SEIRIOS is introduced

articleTitle: Designing Plantar Ortheses via FEM: Model Generation and Multimaterial Insole Testing
publicationTitle: 2024 5th International Conference in Electronic Engineering, Information Technology & Education (EEITE)
abstract: Foot disorders comprise a great variety of pathologies related to one of the most complex joints of the human body. Although surgery is in most cases an effective solution, less invasive solutions like the use of insoles are common in podiatry treatments. The study of the foot structure and via Finite Element Method (FEM) have demonstrated to be very useful to understand different aspects of its behaviour and associated pathologies. A procedure to generate individualized models of real patients, and insoles adapted to the specific pathology could be used as a new tool in podiatry. This, combined with 3D printing, would allow to print the insoles once tested, reducing the time of insole development and fabrication. Two different insoles were tested, analyzing the influence of materials in foot elastic strain, demonstrating that with an adequate foot model, the effect of different materials and insole shapes can be detected with FEM, adapting them to a particular pathology.

articleTitle: Bias Detection and Correction Methods for Machine Learning Algorithms
publicationTitle: 2024 5th International Conference in Electronic Engineering, Information Technology & Education (EEITE)
abstract: Machine learning algorithms are powerful tools for solving complex problems and making data-driven decisions. However, they can also inherit or amplify biases from the data, the design, or the deployment of the algorithms, leading to unfair or discriminatory outcomes for certain groups or individuals. In this paper, we review the sources, types, and measures of bias in machine learning algorithms, and survey the existing methods for detecting and correcting bias at different stages of the algorithmic pipeline. We also discuss the challenges and limitations of these methods, and highlight some open questions and future directions for research on bias in machine learning algorithms.

articleTitle: e-Invoicing Provider Services in Greece: New Perspectives and Weaknesses
publicationTitle: 2024 5th International Conference in Electronic Engineering, Information Technology & Education (EEITE)
abstract: In this paper, authors present the functionality and technical specifications of the Greek Electronic Invoicing Provider Services and examine the standard legal framework from a technical point of view, highlighting the weaknesses of the later based on common practices of the market and identifying possible hacks that can lead to tax evasion.

articleTitle: ONCO-AICO: An AI-Based Educational Tool for Polyp Detection from Colonoscopy
publicationTitle: 2024 5th International Conference in Electronic Engineering, Information Technology & Education (EEITE)
abstract: Despite being the gold standard screening tool for colorectal cancer (CRC), colonoscopies suffer from significant miss rates for polyps and adenomas, influenced by various factors including the experience of colonoscopists. In addition, due to the increasing demand for CRC screening, cost-effective solutions to increase the screening capacity of health care institutions explore the potential role of non-physician colonoscopists, such as nurse practitioners. To increase the detection rates for polyps and adenomas among senior and junior colonoscopists, the ED-funded ONCOSCREEN project proposes integrating artificial intelligence (AI) with existing colonoscopy procedures to educate on polyp detection and mitigate human error. The project introduces the ONCO-AICO tool, a web-based platform, through which trainees can annotate colonoscopy videos, with AI providing real-time feedback and suggestions and Explainable AI (XAI) delivering transparent and reliable support for colonoscopy training. By harnessing AI advancements and fostering collaboration, ONCOSCREEN seeks to revolutionize CRC screening and contribute to better patient outcomes.

articleTitle: Incorporation of Nanodroplets into Semiconducting Polymer Layers to Improve the Performance of Organic Electrolyte-Gated Transistors
publicationTitle: 2024 5th International Conference in Electronic Engineering, Information Technology & Education (EEITE)
abstract: Organic electrolyte-gated transistors (OEGTs) used as a high-capacitance electrolyte dielectric for low-voltage electronics often exhibit the phenomenon of unintentional electrochemical doping (i.e., ion migration throughout the semiconductor) that degrades the device due to ion penetration into the semiconductor layer. Here, we describe a simple method to fabricate a semiconducting polymer layer by incorporating ionic liquid nanodroplets to reduce ion migration into the active (semiconductor) layer. We use poly(3-hexylthiophene) (P3HT) as a semiconducting polymer layer and butyl-3-methylimidazolium tricyanomethanide ionic liquid (BMIM-TCM) as a gate insulator. P3HT semiconductor dissolved in trichlorobenzene (TCB) is cast from a mother solution mixed with a small amount of ionic liquid (IL) dissolved in chloroform (CF) as a nanodroplet component. IL nanodroplets dispersed in P3HT ensure local charge balance in the active layer and thus reduce slow electrochemical transport processes under applied voltage biases. In this work we show the small hysteresis and threshold voltage compared to a pristine P3HT device without IL nanodroplets.

articleTitle: RF Energy Harvesting from Ambient AM Radio Broadcasting Signals for Low-Power Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 5th International Conference in Electronic Engineering, Information Technology & Education (EEITE)
abstract: The implementation of an RF-EH system by ambient AM radio broadcasting signals utilization for IoT selfpowered applications is presented in this study. The system operation took place in the area of Heraklion, Crete, Greece, taking advantage of receiving AM radio transmissions from countries in the Middle East, South Africa, and the Balkans. The proposed AM harvester consists of a long copper wire antenna, an LC tuning circuit, a germanium (1N34A) diodebased doubler rectifier, and a storage capacitor driven by the commercial DC-DC boost converter BQ22504 enable for powering low-consumption devices such as a medical thermometer, a portal calculator or IoT-based sensors.

articleTitle: A Dual Band Graphene Based Concentric Octagon Ring Resonator for Terahertz Sensing
publicationTitle: 2024 5th International Conference in Electronic Engineering, Information Technology & Education (EEITE)
abstract: This proposed work introduces a graphene-based concentric octagon ring resonator for terahertz sensing. The design comprises four layers: a bottom layer of gold metallic material, followed by a silicon dioxide, a thin graphene sheet, and finally, a n upper layer consisting o f three o ctagonal ring resonators. This metamaterial absorber provides two prominent peaks with absorption rates of 99.78% and 94.9% at frequencies of 3.709 THz and 3.876 THz, respectively, with a Fermi energy of 0.3 e V. The quality factor of the structure is calculated to be 537.53 and 1490.76, respectively, at the two resonance frequen-cies, accompanied by Figure of Merit (FoM) values of 395.415 and 1059.64, respectively-both notably high for sensing applications. By adjusting the external voltage to modulate the Fermi energy of the graphene sheet, the absorption rate of the proposed absorber can be finely tuned. The resonance frequency's dependence on the refractive index of the medium becomes particularly pronounced when the Fermi energy of the graphene is set to 0.3 e V. Precise control over the absorption properties of the graphene-based absorber can be achieved in response to changes in the refractive index of the surrounding medium within the specified range n = 1.30 to 1.40. The sensitivity of the sensor is determined to be 2.728 THz/RIU and 2.755 THzlRIU at frequencies of 3.709 THz and 3.876 THz, respectively, where RIU denotes Refractive Index Unit. The proposed absorber demonstrates potential applications in terahertz biomedical sensing.

articleTitle: Gesture Recognition on Textile-Based Pressure Sensor Array
publicationTitle: 2024 5th International Conference in Electronic Engineering, Information Technology & Education (EEITE)
abstract: Wearable technologies are in pursuit of designing portable devices worn by people. In this paper, gesture recognition on a sleeve having a capacitive textile-based pressure sensor array has been developed. Machine learning models are generated to recognize a set of gestures by accumulating capacitance values read from a sensor array during the execution of gestures. The performance of the gesture recognition system is evaluated in the experiments conducted with human test subjects. Real-time gesture prediction is achieved using the trained model. The performed gestures and predicted data are collected and analyzed, resulting in accuracies up to 86'.

articleTitle: Innovation Approaches in CAD Systems Training Program
publicationTitle: 2024 5th International Conference in Electronic Engineering, Information Technology & Education (EEITE)
abstract: The advancements in information technology and computer-aided design have paved the way for virtual modeling and exploration of real-life objects. In the realm of CAD systems, there are subgroups of specialized software (CADCAM- CAE systems) that are designed to accomplish specific object-oriented tasks. Such software is primarily used for mathematical computations, analytic studies of schematic technical objects, and 2D and 3D systems for engineering design practices.

articleTitle: Integration of 3D Printed Heating Systems and Pressure Sensors into Smart Shoes
publicationTitle: 2024 5th International Conference in Electronic Engineering, Information Technology & Education (EEITE)
abstract: Focused on advancing the capabilities of footwear technology, this research endeavors to seamlessly integrate a heating system and pressure sensors into smart shoes. Through meticulous exploration and experimentation, we delve into the fabrication of specimens tailored to accommodate these innovative features. Leveraging the versatile properties of FilaFlex Conductive, we meticulously assess various dimensions and intricate printing patterns to optimize functionality and performance. Our optimization efforts are centered on striking a delicate balance between temperature levels and user comfort within the heating system. Additionally, we conduct a thorough examination of diverse printing patterns to discern their efficacy in enhancing sensor resistance and precision in pressure measurement. To ensure uninterrupted functionality, we engineer a power board equipped with a rechargeable battery, thus completing the integrated system. Upon rigorous testing and analysis, our findings underscore the superior efficiency of specific printing patterns in facilitating precise pressure detection. Building upon these insights, we propose an optimal design paradigm for the integration of heating systems and pressure sensors within smart footwear. By establishing these foundational principles, our work lays the groundwork for the development of next-generation smart shoes endowed with sophisticated heating capabilities and advanced pressure monitoring functionalities.

articleTitle: K-12 Agile Learning with Educational Software and Robotics Technology
publicationTitle: 2024 5th International Conference in Electronic Engineering, Information Technology & Education (EEITE)
abstract: This article discusses the application of agile learning Scrum sprints targeted to K-12 primary education students using educational robotics. Educational robotics are a suitable tool for learning via experimentation, trial & error and retrial, which when inflicted in a form of game-play becomes pleasantly adopted by the students. This has been conducted by implementing carefully designed cumulative sprints which are repeating a certain agile learning process that breaks a larger problem into smaller parts/milestones, designing algorithms as to how to proceed step-by step towards solving the larger overall problem. This is done by evaluating and re-evaluating the progress of every step, until an outcome has been reached and reflected upon. The aforementioned process applies both and equally to tutors and students, individually and as team members, respectfully. Results of the application of agile learning in K-12 educational robotics demonstrate the ability of young K-12 students to cope and realize educational robotics construction, system understanding and algorithm design and implementation via Scratch 3 programming.

articleTitle: Biometrics Data Space: Ensuring Trustworthy and Secure Data Exchange for Suspect Identification
publicationTitle: 2024 5th International Conference in Electronic Engineering, Information Technology & Education (EEITE)
abstract: Concerns about privacy protection, ethics, and the urgency to adhere to EU regulations for personal data protection are increasing as digital biometric technologies are widely being adopted in order to improve the accuracy of the identification and verification processes. This paper proposes the formation of a Biometrics Data Space, a trusted ecosystem that is based on the Data Spaces technology and offers secure sharing and exchange capabilities of biometric data in potential use cases, such as foreign Law Enforcement Agencies (LEAs) and forensic agencies, with an aim to facilitate the process of reliable identification of the suspects. The suggested identification framework incorporates Privacy Enhancing Technologies (PETs), such as homomorphic encryption, to address data protection concerns. Moreover, Large-Scale Data Indexing is applied to the biometric data to provide a fast and efficient comparison o fag iven facial image with ones stored in owners' local premises and without disclosing any personal information during the search and match process. Furthermore, automated access rights control is implemented by Blockchain Smart Contracts that are integrated into the Biomet-rics Data Space framework. The main objective of the suggested framework is to offer a reliable and automated identification system that ensures trust, data sovereignty, interoperability, and robust data protection.

articleTitle: Large Language Models in Modern Forensic Investigations: Harnessing the Power of Generative Artificial Intelligence in Crime Resolution and Suspect Identification
publicationTitle: 2024 5th International Conference in Electronic Engineering, Information Technology & Education (EEITE)
abstract: Large Language Models (LLMs) have recently captured the attention of the scientific c ommunity. S ince t he global launch of LLM-based chatbots in late 2022, the field h as witnessed a rapid increase in interest from researchers, technology providers and citizens alike. With its wide-ranging applicability, Generative Artificial I ntelligence (GenAI) h as t he p otential to impact various aspects of society, from improving communication and accessibility to transforming industries such as healthcare, education and security. More specifically, in the field of Forensic Science, LLMs could offer significant b enefits as sisting Law Enforcement Agencies (LEAs) and Forensic Practitioners in crime investigations. This paper proposes the implementation of a Retrieval Augmented Generation (RAG) LLM, trained with criminology data, to provide swift and actionable insights into specific incidents, thereby enhancing Forensic Data Analysis and facilitating the daily operations of LEAs.

articleTitle: Illicit object detection in X-ray images using Vision Transformers
publicationTitle: 2024 5th International Conference in Electronic Engineering, Information Technology & Education (EEITE)
abstract: Illicit object detection is a critical task performed at various high-security locations, including airports, train stations, subways, and ports. The continuous and tedious work of examining thousands of X-ray images per hour can be mentally taxing. Thus, Deep Neural Networks (DNNs) can be used to automate the X-ray image analysis process, improve efficiency a nd alleviate t he security o fficers' in spection burden. The neural architectures typically utilized in relevant literature are Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs), with Vision Transformers (ViTs) rarely employed. In order to address this gap, this paper conducts a comprehensive evaluation of relevant ViT architectures on illicit item detection in X-ray images. This study utilizes both Transformer and hybrid backbones, such as SWIN and NextViT, and detectors, such as DINO and RT-DETR. The results demonstrate the remarkable accuracy of the DINO Transformer detector in the low-data regime, the impressive real-time performance of YOLOv8, and the effectiveness of the hybrid NextViT backbone.

articleTitle: The Future of Privacy: A Review on AI's Role in Shaping Data Security
publicationTitle: 2024 5th International Conference in Electronic Engineering, Information Technology & Education (EEITE)
abstract: The rapid adoption of Artificial Intelligence (AI) technological advances marked an era of exceptional growth, significantly converting how we interact with the world of technology. But this adoption has arrived at an enormous cost: the gradual loss of private life. The study starts with an indepth investigation into the complicated and modifying relationship between AI and privacy, acquiring information via case studies in the natural environment. One prominent case study is deploying AI technology to recognize faces in public spaces. Issues around illicit tracking and privacy intrusions have grown as governments and business entities regularly employ such technologies for recognition and protection. Assessing the challenges and findings associated with such deployments offers the conceptual debate a practical setting. It explores the various challenges that arise from AIdriven innovations and offers fresh strategies for maintaining and safeguarding individual privacy concerns in emerging data-centric circumstances. It emphasizes AI's dual role as a catalyst for outstanding outcomes and a potential risk to personal privacy. Finally, this study is interested in contributing to the current discussion on AI and Privacy, by providing an in-depth examination of the difficulties that might be utilized by lawmakers, stakeholders in the industry, as well as individuals alike. As humanity moves into a scenario where AI encompasses every aspect of daily life, the study acts as a guide for managing the evolving terrain concerning confidentiality in the era of AI, assisting appropriate AI advancement and preserving human privacy rights.

articleTitle: An Authenticated Method for a Secure Changing Password
publicationTitle: 2024 5th International Conference in Electronic Engineering, Information Technology & Education (EEITE)
abstract: Despite their age, passwords are still widely used more than ever. In many cases, it is the solution that best fits the usage scenario. Researchers are proposing innovative designs and methods to support these scenarios. Many systems, especially sensitive ones, need to change the password. Classic systems rely on changing passwords in two stages, the first i s authentication, which usually consists of two or three rounds, and the second is creating a new password (PW), which also consists of two or three rounds. In this paper, a hidden transmission of a new random PW using the previous one is presented, we talk about an authenticated changing of PW. The verifier g enerates half of the new password and sends it to the prover, the prover authenticates the sent message using the old PW and then returns the authentication proof. After checking it, the verifier creates the second half of the PW. The proposed method combines the authentication and change PW processes into one process consisting of 3 rounds. Therefore, the proposal facilitates the process of automatic periodic change of PW between two entities (user, app, system, etc). Analysis and experiments show that our technique is robust, lightweight, and reduces many potential risks in the field.

articleTitle: Leveraging Industrial IoT Infrastructure for Remote Sensing and Edge Computing in the Mining Sector
publicationTitle: 2024 5th International Conference in Electronic Engineering, Information Technology & Education (EEITE)
abstract: Mining 4.0 signifies a paradigm shift within the mining sector and is defined as an all-encompassing strategy for industry revolution by optimizing mining processes through the utilization of digital technologies, automation, and data analytics to streamline processes. Mining 4.0 aims to develop intelligent and networked mining systems that enhance resource utilization, improve operational efficiency, reduce costs, and mitigate environmental harm, all while prioritizing the safety and welfare of workers. The process of mining digitization encompasses the methodical collection, management, and monitoring of data derived from diverse sources, including sensors, equipment, vehicles, and more. It permits remote, realtime monitoring of environmental and operational conditions, as well as the integration of control systems designed to optimize and automate processes. With digital transformation, the mining sector aspires to overcome conventional obstacles and adjust to changing market requirements, therefore facilitating a more sustainable and efficient future. A critical challenge in the process of digitizing the mining sector is the need to provide reliable routes for transmitting and communicating data between physical and digital components within mining environments. This paper examines the convergence of Mining 4.0 and mining digitization, with a specific emphasis on the pivotal role that remote sensing, edge computing, and decentralized communication systems play in data transmission and real-time monitoring in light of enhancing mining operations' safety and efficiency. The study performed puts forward a European solution based on open standards and tools, revolving around an Industrial Internet of Things (IIoT) Gateway that is a core component of the proposed communication system. This gateway will function as an intermediary between the edge and cloud-based platforms and will facilitate real-time monitoring through the establishment of resilient wireless communication channels, thus leveraging predictive maintenance, and enhancing operational efficiency and worker safety.

articleTitle: A Tethered Unmanned Aircraft System for Crowd Dynamics and Unusual Pattern Extraction
publicationTitle: 2024 5th International Conference in Electronic Engineering, Information Technology & Education (EEITE)
abstract: Unusual pattern extraction and crowd dynamics and analysis has been receiving a constantly growing attention in the recent years contributing to safety, crisis management and situational awareness applications. Traditional video-based systems in this field that are exclusively monitored by human agents, are error-prone and present limited human performance. In this context, the design and implementation of an integrated tethered Unmanned Aircraft System (tUAS), namely INtelligentUxV Surveillance-Unusual Pattern Extraction (INUS-UPE) platform for crowd dynamics and unusual pattern extraction is presented. The INUS-UPE platform adopts a combination of key features and state-of-theart technologies such real-time processing in the edge, videobased pattern analysis for object detection, multiple object tracking, and unusual pattern extraction, web-based user interface (UI) for visualization and possibility of information sharing related the extracted events to external systems such common operational pictures (COPs), Command & Control (C2) platforms, and Human Machine Interfaces (HMIs).

articleTitle: Problem-Solving Through Pair-Programming: The Mediational Role of ChatGPT
publicationTitle: 2024 5th International Conference in Electronic Engineering, Information Technology & Education (EEITE)
abstract: In this study the pair computational problem-solving between the student and ChatGPT was analyzed. The three university students who were experienced in using Python program in computational problem-solving participated in the study. In data collection, a problem involving “limit and sequence” from calculus was used to examine students' collaboration with ChatGPT. Students were asked to construct a program that produces a solution to this problem in Python, and meanwhile, it was stated that they could work in pairs with ChatGPT. The responses provided by ChatGPT to the students in the computational problem-solving were evaluated in both computational and mathematical contexts and a list of cases in which ChatGPT could and could not support students in the computational thinking practices was created. Aside from the incorrect or implicit answers provided by ChatGPT, in general, it was determined that ChatGPT supported the student's performance in computational thinking. It was deduced that it was important for the student to make a rational problem-solving plan and to guide the ChatGPT with the appropriate prompts in order to use rational questioning that leads to productive argumentation with ChatGPT.

articleTitle: Segment Anything Model for Scan-to-Structural Analysis in Cultural Heritage
publicationTitle: 2024 5th International Conference in Electronic Engineering, Information Technology & Education (EEITE)
abstract: Segment anything model (SAM) proposed by META Artificial Intelligence (AI) has disrupted the space of Deep Learning (DL) and Machine Learning (ML) and claims performance that outrivals conventional Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs). The well recognized success of foundation models paved the way towards Natural Language Processing (NLP), which in computer vision domain, rests upon the concept of vision transformers (ViT). The claimed scalability and zero-shot predictability of the proposed mode has spurred extensive research among different fields. In this sense, this paper aims to investigate Segment Anything Model (SAM) potential in cultural heritage (CH) inclined scenarios. This is part of an ongoing project that seeks to implement scan-to-structural analysis at stone level. Based on the findings of this research, SAM zero-shot segmentation ability is quite promising for complex scene understanding. In addition, its tendency to favor small objects may provide a unique opportunity for damage detection and defects classification. Finally, even without any pre-training, SAM exhibits remarkable performance in edge detection and masking, without sacrificing generalizability and its accuracy in segmentation correlates to spatial resolution and background separation.

articleTitle: Fine-Grained Prosody Transfer Text-to-Speech Synthesis with Transformer
publicationTitle: 2024 5th International Conference in Electronic Engineering, Information Technology & Education (EEITE)
abstract: The main goal of this paper is the transfer of expressivity from a reference speech to a synthesized speech. The presented approach conditions the transformer network text to speech synthesis system for transferring prosody from a reference audio utterance to a spoken text. We propose to extend the transformer TTS architecture with a prosody encoder and a multi-head cross-attention block used for fusion and alignment between text and expressivity content. We compare our model to the baseline models of transfer of expressivity namely Global Style Token (GST), Variational AutoEncoder (VAE), and Fine- Grained style control in transformer TTS (FGT). The proposed model shows good prosody transfer and enhances the expressivity and quality of the generated speech as illustrated by listening tests and correlated subjective and objective metrics for evaluating prosody transfer task and naturalness of speech.

articleTitle: The Odysseus Journey Role-Playing Game: Adventures of Rhapsody Λ
publicationTitle: 2024 5th International Conference in Electronic Engineering, Information Technology & Education (EEITE)
abstract: Serious games and game-based learning have revolutionized education by harnessing interactive technologies to enhance engagement and learning outcomes. “Odysseus Journey” is an educational Role-Playing Game (RPG) designed for secondary school students to introduce themselves in the world of Homer's epic, “The Odyssey.” This work explores the integration of classical literature into modern education, allowing students to delve into the cultural contexts of the renowned epic poem. Developed using the Unreal Game Engine, “Odysseus Journey” offers students a dynamic and interactive learning experience that reshapes traditional educational approaches. Furthermore, a study was conducted to evaluate the efficacy of “Odysseus Journey” using the GUESS-18 questionnaire to assess game satisfaction and immersion. The results of the study provide valuable insights into the game's effectiveness in achieving its educational goals and identify areas for further improvement. This research contributes to the ongoing advancement of serious games and their role in shaping the future directions of education.

articleTitle: Exploring Nanorobotics Integration with Microwave and Millimeter-Wave Techniques for Advanced On-wafer Measurement
publicationTitle: 2024 5th International Conference in Electronic Engineering, Information Technology & Education (EEITE)
abstract: In the broader context of the electronics industry, the development of new on-wafer characterization techniques and instruments is imperative for precise validation of circuits designed for high-frequency (HF) applications. Advancing the miniaturization of HF devices necessitates addressing new metrological challenges related to dimensional and electrical characterization. To tackle these challenges, a new fully automated and robotic on-wafer probe station was conceived and constructed from scratch. The measurement probes and the chuck hosting the DUT are mounted on SmarAct® piezoelectric nano-positioners. Integration of a Keysight® Streamline vector network analyzer into the station offers a compact solution close to the probes, reducing non-systematic errors arising from environmental variations. This work is centered on the mechanical aspects necessary for achieving exemplary fine control of probe movements, which are essential for future system automation.

articleTitle: Informative (Dis)information: Exploring the Correlation Between Social Media Disinformation Campaigns and Real-World Criminal Activity
publicationTitle: 2024 5th International Conference in Electronic Engineering, Information Technology & Education (EEITE)
abstract: The connection between online disinformation and crime is a topic of significant i nterest. A n a spect o f t his topic, with strong research potential, is the causal relationship between crimes committed in the real world and disinformation spreading campaigns in the digital world, often on social media platforms. In essence, this research paper focuses on exploring said causal relationship, by seeking to establish a correlation between the diffusion of disinformation, online, and crimes committed offline; specifically, h ate c rimes. F or t his p urpose, a n ovel method was employed: using robust machine learning algorithms for time-series predictions, in order to reveal causal pathways that traditional quantitative techniques may be unable to capture. Thus, the research conducted here exhibits AI applications in social science research and, at the same time, provides a greater understanding of the link between online disinformation and offline crime.

articleTitle: Exploring Machine Learning Algorithms for Infection Detection Using GC-IMS Data: A Preliminary Study
publicationTitle: 2024 5th International Conference in Electronic Engineering, Information Technology & Education (EEITE)
abstract: The developing field of enhanced diagnostic techniques in the diagnosis of infectious diseases, constitutes a crucial domain in modern healthcare. By utilizing Gas Chromatography-Ion Mobility Spectrometry (GC-IMS) data and incorporating machine learning algorithms into one platform, our research aims to tackle the ongoing issue of precise infection identification. Inspired by these difficulties, our goals consist of creating a strong data analytics process, enhancing machine learning (ML) models, and performing thorough validation for clinical applications. Our research contributes to the emerging field of advanced diagnostic technologies by integrating Gas Chromatography-Ion Mobility Spectrometry (GC-IMS) data and machine learning algorithms within a unified Laboratory Information Management System (LIMS) platform. Preliminary trials demonstrate encouraging levels of accuracy when employing various ML algorithms to differentiate between infected and non-infected samples. Con-tinuing endeavors are currently concentrated on enhancing the effectiveness of the model, investigating techniques to clarify its functioning, and incorporating many types of data to further support the early detection of diseases.

articleTitle: Eco-Design Applied to FDM 3D Printing Technology
publicationTitle: 2024 5th International Conference in Electronic Engineering, Information Technology & Education (EEITE)
abstract: The rising accessibility of 3D printing technology, particularly through Fused Deposition Modeling (FDM), is revolutionizing a broad spectrum of fields, ranging from industrial component prototyping to the manufacturing of appliance spare parts and the crafting of domestic tools. Despite these advances, the environmental implications of deploying this technology remain poorly understood. Addressing this gap, a comparative analysis has been conducted on the two predominant filament types utilized within this domain: PolyLactic Acid (PLA) and Acrylonitrile Butadiene Styrene (ABS). This investigation seeks to assess both the mechanical strength and the environmental impact of these materials, taking into account their effects on human toxicity, water, acidification, eutrophication, and global warming. Accordingly, the study involves tensile testing of standardized samples and executes a comprehensive life cycle assessment (LCA), employing the CML-baseline methodology to interconnect the mechanical attributes and environmental impacts of the printed specimens. This approach aims to provide a holistic understanding of the sustainability aspects of FDM technology, facilitating informed decision-making in its application.

articleTitle: Seamless Identity Verification at Water and Land Borders
publicationTitle: 2024 5th International Conference in Electronic Engineering, Information Technology & Education (EEITE)
abstract: Identity verification at water and land borders constitutes a great challenge for Border Authorities and relevant technology providers due to the continuous variability and complexity of the border crossing points. In the meantime, identity fraud continuously evolves requiring novel mechanisms for secure and seamless identity verification. ODYSSEUS introduces a set of novel biometric-based mechanisms that will allow EU citizens that are or not part of the Schengen area to cross the borders across the Member States in a secure and frictionless manner. Seamless identity verification based on facial biometric will perform 1:N matching without requiring from the user to stop at the border. A novel Digital and Virtual passport will allow EU citizens to verify their identity through a mobile wallet, which will be protected through AI-powered continuous behavioural authentication. Each of the technologies will be explained through X-AI for improved result interpretation and reasoning, while the results of each of the technologies will be fused through the Decision Support System (DSS) into an overall identity risk score provided to the Border Authorities. A faceless person counting component will allow Border Authorities to further predict potential queues at the border crossing points and perform relevant adjustments. The platform will be validated in water and land Schengen borders showcasing the increase in productivity and reduction of queues at the borders.

articleTitle: Cybersecurity as a Contributor to United Nations SDGs towards enhancing the ESG Reporting
publicationTitle: 2024 5th International Conference in Electronic Engineering, Information Technology & Education (EEITE)
abstract: This paper investigates the contribution of the var-ious cybersecurity domains to the United Nations' Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs), emphasizing the critical role of cybersecurity in advancing global sustainability efforts. The paper examines how cybersecurity measures and practices can contribute to achieving the SDGs by ensuring the security, resilience, and sustainability of critical systems and infrastructure. Furthermore, it highlights the integration of cybersecurity into Environmental, Social, and Governance (ESG) reporting, enhancing corporate resilience and aligning with SDGs. A use case focused on specific SDG is also analysed and discussed. This analysis offers valuable insights and guidance for incorporating cybersecurity into Environmental, Social, and Governance (ESG) reporting processes, contributing to a more sustainable and resilient future.

articleTitle: Enhancing Industry 4.0 Cybersecurity Training through Cyber Range Platform
publicationTitle: 2024 5th International Conference in Electronic Engineering, Information Technology & Education (EEITE)
abstract: Industry 4.0, the fourth industrial revolution, incorporates advanced technologies like IoT, big data, and AI but increases vulnerability to cyber-attacks. To mitigate these risks, hands-on training on realistic cybersecurity scenarios is necessary. Cyber-range platforms offer virtual training environments to simulate complex cyber threats, allowing security teams to develop and enhance skills safely. These platforms cover incident response, network security, threat intelligence, and digital forensics. Capture-The-Flag events also attract attention in cybersecurity. The study aims to develop a cyber-range platform using open-source tools such as CTFd to create realistic cybersecurity scenarios and propose an interactive industrial training solution. The development platform is an open-source framework called Naumachia. It is a lightweight, secure and containerized infrastructure for creating virtual machines. The training is organized through gamification, involving SQL injection, Snort Ruling, forensic analysis, and man-in-the-middle spoofing. The system is easily expandable and encourages trainees to test defenses and attacks safely. An anonymous survey evaluated the platform's knowledge, training, organization, educational material, and challenges.

articleTitle: Research of Mathematical Model of Microwave Drying of Wet Wool
publicationTitle: 2024 5th International Conference in Electronic Engineering, Information Technology & Education (EEITE)
abstract: The paper considers a mathematical model of microwave drying of wet wool. Based on the analysis of the model, the dependence of the temperature of wet wool irradiated with electromagnetic fields on the duration of exposure and the depth of the sample, the dependence of temperature changes at certain points in time throughout the entire depth of the chamber with wet wool, and the dynamics of temperature changes in each section of the wool volume from the beginning to the end of drying, dependence of temperature changes at certain points in time, dependence of temperature changes throughout the entire volume, dependence of wool moisture content on the density of the incident power and drying time, dependence of the moisture content of washed wool on the level of power density at various points in time during drying, dependence of the moisture content of washed wool on drying time at different power levels

articleTitle: CircuitLib: A Case Study of Spin-Off e-Business in Embedded and Electronic Systems Development
publicationTitle: 2024 5th International Conference in Electronic Engineering, Information Technology & Education (EEITE)
abstract: In this study, the business model of a Spin-Off pilot e-Business activity in embedded and electronic systems development was presented. The proposed e-Business innovation is based on utilizing the existing know-how of the partners, producing innovative and exportable products, and using new ICT technologies. CircuitLib's dominant mission is to create a global people community with common interests in electronic systems technology who will combine their knowledge to make an open-access electronic circuits e-library. The main idea concerns the development of a web-platform serving research, study, design and electronic innovative systems implementation while supporting at the same time the provision of e-Library and online store services. CircuitLib introduces innovation by offering know-how that is freely accessible to the public, setting up a global people community with common interests, exchanging ideas, and using the advantages of online networking. The proposed web-platform aims at attractive, affordable products, exclusivity, as well as the possibilities that ICT give to such a type of business, such as fast service (e-service) and the provision of uninterrupted technical support through customer communication lines (email, chat, web chat, e-forum). The proposed Business Plan includes a complete SWOT Analysis, a Competition Analysis, and an Analysis of the individual BMC building blocks for the sustainability of the e-Business activity.

articleTitle: Enhancing 3D Printing Materials with Biochar: A Literature Review
publicationTitle: 2024 5th International Conference in Electronic Engineering, Information Technology & Education (EEITE)
abstract: This literature review explores the integration of biochar in 3D printing materials, highlighting the enhancements in mechanical and thermochemical properties that biochar composites can offer. Biochar, a byproduct of the thermochemical conversion of biomass, is characterized for its superior porosity, large specific surface area, and carbon richness, making it an ideal additive in sustainable manufacturing practices. This review highlights the potential of biochar-enhanced materials in multiple 3D printing applications, including polymers, metals, ceramics, and fibers. It emphasizes biochar's role in improving the functionality, resilience, and performance of 3D printed parts, while also contributing to environmental sustainability. The challenges are also underlined with the uniform dispersion of biochar within composite materials and the need for specialized printing technologies are also addressed. Overall, integrating biochar into 3D printing materials is nothing but a promising avenue for advancing additive manufacturing technologies while adhering to ecological and performance standards.

articleTitle: A Methodology for Applying Decision Policies into Smart Buildings with the use of Computational Argumentation and IoT Technologies
publicationTitle: 2024 5th International Conference in Electronic Engineering, Information Technology & Education (EEITE)
abstract: This paper reports on our work for defining a methodology for applying energy and other polices into smart buildings that use Internet of Things enabled devices. The goal is to automate decisions on a variety of issues where there is a conflict of policies between the priorities of different users and roles. We use computational argumentation and a method for compiling meta-policies to automate the decision-making process with the capability to offer human-readable explanations and, at the same time, to achieve increased energy efficiency. IoT sensors take the necessary measurements and data using the KNX standard. To validate our methodology we used an energy related scenario. The case study is applied on a building in the Technical University of Crete, where there are suitable sensors for measuring basic parameters (or data), such as temperature, lighting conditions, motion, and, carbon dioxide levels. The building's energy consumption data is imported by the Open StudiolEnergy plus application. A web-based service for hierarchical argumentation, Gorgias Cloud, is used to process the data and make decisions.
